script: A shrimp smaller than your finger makes one of the loudest sounds in the ocean. The pistol shrimp snaps its oversized claw shut incredibly fast. This shoots out a jet of water that forms a bubble. When the bubble collapses, it makes a loud crack that can stun small prey. Scientists estimate the inside of the bubble briefly reaches thousands of degrees. Big groups of these shrimp crackle so loudly they can interfere with submarine sonar.
